- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes, followed by mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly after a spike in the middle.
- Forecast bias is stronger when historical prices are rising; model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates true decline until 10–15 days later.
- When true price falls sharply after a peak, model continues to hold high forecasts for 5–7 days longer than actual.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike excessively in response to minor price movements.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 5–10% for periods with recent downward momentum or mean-reversion signals.
- Model tends to ignore long-term trend direction — overestimates if trend is upward, underestimates if downward.
- Correction should be applied to the last 5–7 days of forecast, especially if true outcome shows mean reversion or downward correction.
